title: Surge-aware GPU Safety Margin Calculator for Mixed Footprints
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We observe recurring transient OOMs and degraded tail latency when tenant-mix shifts toward long-context KV-heavy requests during bursts. Current static headroom targets are conservative (10-15%) for many workloads and overly permissive for heterogeneous mixes, resulting in either wasted capacity or risk of failure in mixed continuous-batching scenarios. Goal: design and implement a lightweight calculator and runtime advisory that produces per-GPU, per-pool safety margins (headroom) that account for weighted probability of surge classes, model weight permanency, and on-peak KV retention pressure. The calculator will be used by autoscaler policies, the headroom advisor in the scheduler, and capacity planning dashboards.
motivation_and_success_criteria: Reduce transient OOM incidents by 70% for mixed-tenant bursts; keep average reserved headroom <= 12% across fleet when workloads are stable; provide clear telemetry so ops can explain headroom changes to customers. Success measured by: (1) production incident rate delta, (2) percent of GPUs with headroom above target, (3) cost delta for reserved capacity after rollout.
design_summary: Calculator inputs: per-tenant request-size distribution, KV retention ratio (KV tokens / sequence tokens), model weight residency (static/dynamically offloaded), observed microburst rate, batch shape histogram, and quantization profile. Outputs: safety_margin_percent, recommended_kv_eviction_threshold, temporary-weight-offload-suggested, and a confidence_score. Implementation staged: (A) offline simulator (Python) that runs historical traces to generate parameterized margin maps; (B) a runtime microservice that ingests telemetry and serves margin recommendations via gRPC to scheduler; (C) scheduler integration to convert margin -> soft preemption buckets and autoscaler hints.
technical_decisions_and_tradeoffs:
- Probabilistic vs deterministic: we favor a probabilistic margin with confidence buckets (P50/P95) which lets higher-tier tenants purchase stricter guarantees. Deterministic floor (min_margin=6%) prevents pathological under-reservation.
- Complexity vs speed: initial simulator uses simplified eviction model and per-tenant weight permanence heuristics to iterate quickly; a follow-on will incorporate exact allocator state.
- Where to enforce: advisor will publish margins but not block requests; enforcement is via scheduler preemption and autoscaler signals to avoid latency cliffs.
rollout_plan: 1) Canary simulator on sample cluster (2 weeks): validate against last 90 days of traces and compare predicted OOMs to observed. 2) Publish advisor API and enable read-only for scheduler (1 week). 3) Enable advisory-driven autoscaler hints for non-critical pools (2 weeks). 4) Progressive enablement for P1 pools and dedicated customers after 4 weeks of stability. 5) Post-rollback hooks enabled for 48h after each step.
telemetry_and_observability: New metrics: headroom_calculated_percent, headroom_confidence, kv_eviction_recommendation_rate, predicted_oom_risk_index. Dashboards: headroom-trends (per-region, per-pool), margin-accuracy (prediction vs realized). Alerts: predicted_oom_risk_index>0.7 sustained for 5m. Logs: advisor decisions include trace_id linking to request histograms for audit.
testing_and_validation:
- Unit tests: input sanitization, margin math, corner cases.
- Integration tests: advisor <-> scheduler gRPC contract mocked.
- Simulation validation: replay historical trace subsets and measure false-negative OOM predictions.
- Load test: synthetic mixed-profile bursts with kv-heavy and short-chat requests to measure headroom efficacy.
docs_and_customer_communication: Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Surge-aware+Headroom+Calculator. Customer note template for Dedicated customers describing headroom mechanics and opt-out. Changelog entry for runtime-1.20 and guidance in ops-runbook (links included in PRD).
implementation_notes:
- Python simulator repo: github.com/redwood-inference/headroom-sim (draft branch).
- Runtime service in Go (minimal dependencies) with a Redis-backed parameter cache for quick lookups.
- Scheduler shim to be added to pool-controller component, toggled via feature flag 'headroom_advisor_v1'.
- Telemetry ingestion will hook to existing metrics pipeline and add a small Prometheus exporter.
open_questions: What is the minimum SLA tier that should get deterministic margins?
How much historical window provides stable predictions for new tenants?
Should we expose tenant-level recommendations to customers or keep advisory internal?
